Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:
Googled, didn't see an answer, so...

My Stanislava has a secure haven on her, but foolishly gets sent into
torpor anyway during a combat.

Now, normally, if one of my minions attempts to rescue or diablerize
another one of my minions, that's an undirected action -- my
prey/predator can block.

So, the question is: Can my own minions rescue or diablerize Stanislava,
or is still considered a (D) action?

--Colin McGuigan

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


The haven is burned when Stanislave foolishly got sent to torpor.
Card text:"Burn this card if this minion enters torpor."

But rescuing your own vampire is not directed, correct.

> Card text:"Burn this card if this minion enters torpor."
>
> But rescuing your own vampire is not directed, correct.

Also note that, while Stanislava doesn't keep her Secure Haven if sent
to torpor, you can play a Secure Haven on a Stanislava who is *already*
in torpor and it won't burn itself. (Card text only requires being
played on a minion you control, not a *ready* minion.) And then it
would matter that your own rescue/diablerie attempts are not directed.
(This actually mattered in a game I played a while ago, where my prey
played Secure Haven on a vamp he had in torpor and then was sad because
his cross-table ally was prohibited from rescuing the vampire, which he
would otherwise have done to help him out. :-)

Just FYI, the "actions that affect your own stuff are undirected" rule
is in the rulebook: 6.2.2 section 1 "Who May Attempt to Block".

Josh
